title: EcoSentinel
speaker: Mario
cue: Point to the photograph, then pause after the question
speech: Suppose we upload this photograph and ask what the animal eats. Where should the answer come from? EcoSentinel connects the image to stored wildlife evidence and lets us inspect the sources behind the response. We will show the engineering that makes this possible.

title: A photograph starts the investigation
speaker: Mario
cue: The domain gives the pipeline a purpose
speech: Our use case is a shared wildlife collection for education and biodiversity exploration. Someone can start with a photograph, find related recordings and descriptions, and ask a question grounded in those documents. We chose Iberian fauna to keep that investigation concrete.

title: Three modalities, one reference dataset
speaker: Mario
cue: Counts describe the reference installation
speech: Our reference dataset contains one hundred images, thirty-four recordings and sixty-four texts across ten Iberian species. Wikimedia, Xeno-canto, Wikipedia and GBIF provide the source material. Availability is uneven: the lizard has no audio. We retain that gap and preserve attribution rather than inventing missing observations.

title: The EcoSentinel pipeline
speaker: Mario
cue: Follow the boundaries and the source references
speech: The orchestrator runs sixteen steps across four zones and finishes with reconciliation. Landing preserves originals. Formatted establishes file representations. Trusted makes quality decisions. Exploitation creates searchable vectors. The first three zones use S3-compatible storage in Docker; Chroma stores the vectors. Queries open a verified copy of that persistent index to protect the audited original from internal database writes. After data updates, we explicitly refresh the copy.

title: Hashes and embeddings
speaker: Mario
cue: A byte fingerprint and a similarity representation answer different questions
speech: We use two representations for different jobs. SHA-two-fifty-six fingerprints the file bytes. It helps verify integrity and build deterministic identities. An embedding represents features learned by a particular model, so nearby vectors can retrieve related content. Recompressing a photograph changes its bytes and therefore its hash, while its embedding may remain similar. That is a conceptual example, not a new measurement. Landing uses a hash prefix and filename for ingestion identity. Similarity search uses embeddings. A high similarity score does not establish an exact copy or confirm a species.

title: Landing identity and completion records
speaker: Mario
cue: Technical reuse has explicit conditions
speech: Landing gives each ingestion a deterministic key: the first sixteen hexadecimal characters of SHA-two-fifty-six, followed by the original filename. Same bytes and filename produce the same key. Before uploading, we check whether that object already exists in Temporal. If Temporal is absent, a separate completion record points to its Persistent copy. We check that target and the source identity before skipping the upload. Promotion writes completion only after verifying the copied bytes. A missing target or conflicting identity produces an error. A renamed copy gets a different ingestion key, so Trusted handles content duplicates separately. The marker confirms Persistent promotion; later reconciliation checks the downstream state.

title: Landing: four identity cases
speaker: Mario
cue: Read each incoming photo against the already-seen photo; names are illustrative
speech: These four cases show what technical deduplication means. Assume the source metadata matches and the first file is already recorded. Same bytes and same filename reuse the existing key, so there is no new upload. Identical bytes under another name create a new key and enter Landing. Different bytes under the same name also enter: their hash changes, so the original is not overwritten. If both change, the file enters too. Landing prevents repeated technical ingestion. Trusted still checks content duplicates and perceptual similarity. A recompressed photograph can pass Landing even when it looks unchanged.

title: Formatted choices for wildlife data
speaker: Mario
cue: Explain what each choice preserves and what it costs
speech: For wildlife photographs, RGB JPEG gives us a compact, widely supported representation. Quality ninety-five prioritises visual fidelity. It remains lossy; PNG would preserve pixels and transparency instead. We keep dimensions and leave model cropping to Exploitation. Six real multiframe image sources required an explicit primary-frame policy. Audio becomes FLAC PCM sixteen: compressed PCM avoids another lossy audio encode, while preserving rate, channels and duration when possible. Higher-precision input can lose precision through quantisation. UTF-eight, consistent line endings and Unicode normalisation keep Spanish and English text readable across platforms. Text extraction loses layout. Persistent Landing keeps every complete original. Sambhav will explain the quality decisions.

title: Trusted: rejection or warning?
speaker: Sambhav
cue: Separate hard failures from useful ecological variation
speech: Our Trusted policy separates rejection from warnings. Images must decode and respect a twenty-megabyte, forty-megapixel budget, with at least one hundred and twenty-eight pixels per side. Pixel count matters because compressed size alone does not bound decoding cost. Audio has a two-hundred-megabyte ceiling and text has four. These are operational budgets. Exact hashes detect identical image bytes; perceptual candidates need structural and colour confirmation. Watermark signals and quiet recordings remain visible warnings. Quiet intervals can carry ecological meaning. A later rejection or storage error preserves an earlier accepted object and records the reason for review.

title: Quality decisions leave an audit trail
speaker: Sambhav
cue: Show the actual report and distinguish completeness from truth
speech: Each asset receives a quality manifest. We aggregate those records into HTML, CSV, JSON and plots. This is our recorded image report: all one hundred images remain, including thirty-two possible watermark warnings. Complete provenance fields establish traceability, not biological correctness.

title: Did filtering change species representation?
speaker: Sambhav
cue: Before and after measure the effect of our policy
speech: We compare species distributions before and after Trusted because filtering could alter what users retrieve. Here, both series remain at ten images per species and the measured distribution shift is zero. This describes our small curated sample, not the distribution of wildlife populations.

title: Quiet intervals remain in the evidence
speaker: Sambhav
cue: The warning has an explicit consequence
speech: Nine recordings have a high proportion of low-energy windows. We retain all thirty-four recordings, so the distributions before and after match. Removing quiet sections could erase distant calls or environmental context. The warning tells a reviewer what to inspect without rewriting the recording.

title: Five collections, 6,021 embeddings
speaker: Sambhav
cue: Completeness is more than a row count
speech: Long recordings and documents produce several segments, which explains how one hundred and ninety-eight assets generate six thousand and twenty-one vectors. Each vector retains its source, asset identity, segment position and model-policy contract. Compatible reruns check exact segment coverage before reusing results. Counts alone are insufficient: a duplicated segment could hide a missing one. This contract lets us detect and recover incomplete publication without recomputing every embedding.

title: Three encoders, three relationships
speaker: Sambhav
cue: Model choice follows the retrieval relationship
speech: For an image and a sentence, CLIP uses separate encoders trained to place related content in one shared space. CLAP does the same for sounds and descriptions, without treating animal calls as speech. Multilingual E-five small retrieves passages in Spanish and English. These pretrained models support our CPU deployment. Within each compatible space, we can compare vectors. Across different models, we combine their result positions using reciprocal rank fusion, rather than compare raw scores. Equal vector dimensions do not make spaces interchangeable. English descriptions generally suit CLAP better. We have not established which model is best on a labelled wildlife benchmark.

title: Similarity is an angle, not a probability
speaker: Sambhav
cue: The two-dimensional calculation illustrates the actual normalised-vector rule
speech: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors. We divide their dot product by their lengths. Our vectors are normalised, so the calculation becomes a dot product. In this two-dimensional example, the query is one, zero. The first candidate scores zero point nine six, the second zero point six, and the third zero. The first is most aligned; zero means perpendicular. Our actual vectors have hundreds of dimensions. Higher scores mean closer representations within that space. There is no universal cut-off for relevant wildlife, and zero point nine six is not ninety-six percent confidence.

title: Finding neighbours: HNSW in Chroma
speaker: Sambhav
cue: Cosine scores a pair; HNSW selects neighbours through a layered graph
speech: The lecture distinguishes a similarity measure from a search algorithm. Cosine scores two vectors. To find neighbours among many vectors, our Chroma collections configure H-N-S-W: Hierarchical Navigable Small World. Its sparse upper layers make longer hops; denser lower layers refine the candidate neighbourhood. This is approximate search, so it can miss a true nearest neighbour. We use the database implementation and have not measured its recall on labelled wildlife queries. Our code also has an exact path for at most sixty-four eligible vectors. It compares all of them directly, avoiding a dependency on a persisted graph for tiny or newly created collections.

title: Task 1: a real image query
speaker: Sambhav
cue: Point out both the useful matches and the failure
speech: This is a recorded image query using real CLIP embeddings. We exclude the entire reference asset and group segments by file. The slide shows matches at ranks one and three from five returned assets. Four catalogue labels are lynx and one is wolf; a cropped variant also survives. These results demonstrate retrieval and expose the limits of visual similarity. A high score does not verify species identity or prove that every near duplicate has been removed.

title: Task 2: one query, images and text
speaker: Sambhav
cue: One query returns different modalities
speech: This text query returned four images and four texts. The illustrated image scores zero point three three two. It is a useful candidate despite scoring much lower than our image-to-image example. Query type changes the score distribution; one threshold would mislead. A diversity policy prevents text passages dominating the display. Users choose top-k from one to fifty; eight is the default, counting distinct assets. Wassim will show how retrieved evidence supports generation.

title: Task 3: answer from retrieved evidence
speaker: Wassim
cue: Retrieval, generation and post-validation remain separate
speech: Task three retrieves evidence before asking Qwen to generate an answer. For image questions, CLIP retrieves visual candidates and BLIP supplies an unverified caption. E-five retrieves relevant text; we pass bounded evidence units with explicit identifiers to Qwen. The three-billion-parameter quantised model runs locally on CPU. It receives text rather than image pixels, which controls memory but loses visual detail. After generation, we validate allowed source identifiers and literal quotations. This does not prove every interpretation is correct. We distinguish supported answers, partial answers and abstention from technical failures such as timeouts.

title: The frog case: evidence and uncertainty
speaker: Wassim
cue: A candidate remains a hypothesis
speech: The recorded frog case answered habitat and diet using source excerpts. The interface exposes both the candidate species and the quotations. We keep the photographic identification uncertain. A separate complete-genome request produced an abstention because the required evidence was absent. These examples test the behaviour of the full model pipeline. They are qualitative cases, not a biological accuracy benchmark. We use the recording here because CPU generation can take minutes.

title: The second run adds zero new vectors
speaker: Wassim
cue: The full CLI has been exercised twice
speech: We also tested the complete command-line pipeline with isolated storage and real CPU models. Three synthetic assets produced seven vectors on the first run. The second completed all sixteen steps with zero new vectors. Reconciliation checked the resulting state. This demonstrates compatible reuse across the zones. The image is noise and the audio is a tone, so this execution test does not measure wildlife relevance.

title: How we tested the pipeline
speaker: Wassim
cue: Name the failure and the state we assert afterwards
speech: Our validation has several layers. Three hundred and sixty-four offline tests use generated inputs to check contracts and failure paths. The isolated integration test runs real zone code with S3 and Chroma twice, using deterministic encoders. Separate native CPU runs check the actual model path. We inject copy mismatches, failed completion records and incomplete vector publication, then verify that retries preserve accepted data and recover missing work. Search tests check grouping, filters and exclusion of the reference. The new browser check follows top-k through real HTTP requests. The tests assert resulting state, not simply that a command returned successfully.

title: An input can fail before it reaches storage
speaker: Wassim
cue: The executable header is harmless test data
speech: Here, a file called lynx dot jpg contains a harmless Windows executable header. Our Security Gate blocks it before hashing or upload; we never execute it. Other generated cases cover corrupt files, empty inputs, archive expansion and resource limits. A controlled watermark signal verifies the opposite outcome: retain the image and record a warning. Combined statement coverage is seventy-one point eight two percent. It measures code exercised, not retrieval accuracy. This screening does not replace antivirus.

title: A query with a traceable answer
speaker: Wassim
cue: Return to the opening question
speech: We began by asking where an answer should come from. EcoSentinel makes that route inspectable: source material, explicit transformations, quality decisions and retrieved evidence. Our next evaluation needs expert-labelled relevance and answers, including cases where the system abstains unnecessarily.
